title: Marketplace Orders: Each Order Stands on Its Own Record
content:
**Clause.** A buyer may hold any number of Marketplace Orders orders at the same time, in any delivery option and with any number of sellers. Every order is its own record: its charges, returns, refunds, replacements and Northloop Guarantee claims are computed on that order alone and are never pooled with another order. The only buyer-level figure that reads across orders is the buyer's remorse-return history used by the return history policy.

There is no maximum number of orders per buyer.

## The same rule, by question

| Question | Answer under the clause |
|---|---|
| Is there a cap on how many open orders a buyer may hold? | No; any number, on any delivery option, with any number of sellers. |
| Does a refund booked on one order reduce what is owed on another? | No; every amount is computed on its own order. |
| Can two orders share one Northloop Guarantee claim or one replacement? | No; claims and replacements belong to the order they are recorded on. |
| Is anything read across a buyer's orders? | Only the remorse-return history count. |

### Hypothetical illustration

A hypothetical buyer holds two orders from the same seller, one on Seller Fulfilled Standard Shipping and one on Fulfilled by Northloop Two-Day. A return on the first order is refunded from the first order's own figures; the second order's charges and refunds are untouched by it. The two orders are example inputs only.
